title: Interactive Personal Portfolio
description: A five-page portfolio with JSON-powered project cards, live category filters, keyword search, and a persistent color theme.
highlights: Fetches a separate JSON file and creates project cards in JavaScript.
Combines category filtering with case-insensitive keyword search.
Shows project details in a Bootstrap modal and saves a light or dark theme across pages.
learning: Separating content, presentation, and behavior while connecting asynchronous requests to accessible interface updates.

title: Campus Connections
description: A campus events page that organizes student opportunities, resources, and event details with semantic HTML and a custom Flexbox layout.
highlights: Groups three campus events in a Flexbox card layout.
Includes resource links and an in-page navigation menu.
Uses semantic sections, a skip link, and descriptive link labels.
learning: Writing a structured HTML document and using a shared stylesheet to create a consistent layout without a CSS framework.

title: Product Search & Filter
description: A C# console catalog that lets users find products by name, category, maximum price, or availability.
course: MIS 3033 · HWK 1, Problem 4 · Download includes the complete four-project solution.
highlights: Stores 12 products in a collection of Product objects.
Supports partial name matching and case-insensitive category searches.
Filters by an inclusive maximum price or current stock status.
learning: Modeling a simple catalog with a class, iterating through collections, and implementing independent filter functions.

title: Campus Bites
description: A Bootstrap practice site presenting campus dining ideas through a responsive navbar, restaurant cards, and a two-column information section.
course: MIS 4013 · Bootstrap practice · A class exercise with illustrative restaurant content.
highlights: Uses a collapsible Bootstrap navbar and responsive grid columns.
Presents restaurant information in consistent Bootstrap cards.
Practices Bootstrap spacing, buttons, and form-control styling.
learning: Using framework utilities to create responsive structure while keeping presentation in a separate custom stylesheet.

title: Student Course Website
description: An early two-page website introducing my studies, interests, goals, and current courses at the University of Oklahoma.
highlights: Links an About page and a dedicated courses page.
Uses a shared stylesheet and clear navigation between pages.
Includes a campus photograph with attribution and accessible image text.
learning: Organizing a small website, maintaining relative file paths, and keeping navigation and styling consistent across documents.

title: Shipping Calculator
description: A C# console application that calculates delivery charges using order value, shipping method, and rewards membership rules.
course: MIS 3033 · HWK 1, Problem 1 · Download includes the complete four-project solution.
highlights: Supports Standard, Two-Day, and Overnight shipping choices.
Applies free Standard shipping at $75 and a rewards discount to eligible methods.
Rejects invalid input and formats monetary results consistently.
learning: Translating written business requirements into conditional logic and reusable calculation functions.

title: Restaurant Order
description: A C# ordering exercise that stores menu selections and calculates a receipt with a subtotal, discount, and sales tax.
course: MIS 3033 · HWK 1, Problem 2 · Download includes the complete four-project solution.
highlights: Builds an order from a list of MenuItem objects.
Handles repeated selections and an empty order.
Applies a 10% discount at $30 and calculates 8.5% tax after the discount.
learning: Combining classes, collections, and functions to produce a receipt whose displayed amounts reconcile.

title: Account Registration Validator
description: A C# input-validation exercise that checks registration fields and explains every failed rule in one result.
course: MIS 3033 · HWK 1, Problem 3 · Validation exercise; it does not store user accounts. Download includes the complete four-project solution.
highlights: Checks required names, assignment-specific email rules, and an age threshold.
Validates password length, uppercase letters, numbers, and exact confirmation.
Collects validation errors rather than stopping after the first failed rule.
learning: Breaking validation into Boolean functions and giving clear feedback without confusing an exercise with a production authentication system.
